title: New Hires and Staff Updates on Video
summary: Additionally, some good news on three members of the team: Suzanne Hillinger and Mac Schneider, who have been senior producers over the past few months, are now on the team full time.
body_markdown:
Video has several new faces and other staff updates on Reporter Video. Read more from the newsroom’s video director, Solana Pyne, and deputy director, Mona Lalwani.


We are thrilled to welcome some new faces to the Reporter Video team on the Video desk, as well as some additional exciting staff updates.


Joy Sung joined as a video journalist in D.C., where she is producing and editing short-form reporter videos and helping us expand our coverage over the weekends.


Joy spent seven years at The Washington Post, most recently as a senior video journalist focused on local news and enterprise coverage. She collaborated with investigative and visual teams on stories such as America’s assisted-living industry, the Jan. 6 Capitol riot, the fatal 2025 plane crash near Reagan National Airport and the impact of a generational crime surge on D.C. middle schoolers. Prior to The Post, Joy was a multimedia specialist at The Kennedy Center and a freelance documentary filmmaker and photographer.


She holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in television and broadcast journalism from Chapman University and a master’s degree in new media photojournalism from George Washington University.


Chris Whitworth joined the team in New York as a senior video journalist and will help expand our video coverage over the weekends.


Chris joins us from NBC News, where he was a coordinating producer on the “Today” Show, overseeing daily and breaking news coverage and leading production on features. His work included Edward R. Murrow Award-winning coverage of the Oct. 7 attacks in Israel and the assassination attempt on President Donald Trump. Before NBC News, Chris was a writer and producer on Vox’s Emmy-nominated series “Glad You Asked.” He previously freelanced as a video journalist and editor at The Times, where he produced the series “ScienceTake.” Earlier in his career, he spent four years as a producer and editor at The Guardian in London and New York.


Siobhan Lockhart joined as a senior producer in New York,


where


she is overseeing our news and political coverage, while also helping us mobilize on news targets on weekends


.


Siobhan is an Emmy-winning producer with vast experience in news, documentary and nonfiction television. She started her career as a CBS page and went on to work at “CBS News Sunday Morning” and the weekend edition of “The CBS Evening News.” From there, she helped shape series and produced shows for HBO, PBS, MSNBC, National Geographic, Hulu, Prime Video and Showtime. She was part of the Emmy-winning team that made “Science Fair: The Series” for National Geographic and produced high-profile interviews with politicians, business leaders and celebrities for three seasons of “Axios” on HBO.


She holds a master’s degree in television journalism from Goldsmiths, University of London.


Photo Credit: Edward Vega


Marie-Anne Harrigan joined as a video journalist. Based in New York, she will help create visually impactful vertical video series with the Times’s culture and lifestyle reporters.


Before joining The Times, Annie worked as an editorial intern for Billboard, where she covered daily music news from Los Angeles while completing her graduate degree in journalism. Previously, Annie worked across Vox Media’s lifestyle publications Eater, Punch, Thrillist and POPSUGAR. During her time at Vox, Annie moved between operations, editorial and social roles. She produced social videos for Eater, wrote on-site content for all four publications and helped oversee the daily operations of the lifestyle brands.


Hailing from Long Island, Annie is a graduate of Harvard and the University of Southern California’s Annenberg School for Communications and Journalism.


Photo Credit: Edward Vega


Photo Credit: Credit: Earl Wilson


Adrianne Jeffries joined as a senior video journalist, working across investigations and enterprise coverage.


Most recently she was a producer at Bloomberg Originals, where she earned an Emmy for Outstanding Short Documentary, multiple Deadline Club awards, and a SABEW nomination. Previously, she led the investigative reporting on the Netflix series “Broken” and was an associate producer on the Peabody Award-nominated “Predators


*.* ” While reporting for “The Markup,”


her investigative series about Amazon earned a Loeb Award and her series on Google’s monopoly over web search was cited in Congress. She also was a managing editor at Vice’s Motherboard, and has written for The Verge, Businessweek and The Times.


Adrianne graduated from The College of William and Mary with a bachelor’s degree in English.


Photo Credit: Credit: Earl Wilson


Additionally, some good news on three members of the team:


Suzanne Hillinger and Mac Schneider, who have been senior producers over the past few months, are now on the team full time. They have been valuable assets to the team, overseeing the creation of high-priority daily news videos, serving as a go-to resource for colleagues and providing editorial guidance and constructive feedback with collaborators across the newsroom.


Photo Credit: Alexis Johnson


Based in New York, Suzanne works closely with colleagues across the newsroom to identify critical stories and produce reporter videos that provide sharp insight into headline news stories.


Suzanne is an Emmy Award-winning filmmaker with over two decades of experience overseeing documentary films and series that range from investigative to observational. She first worked at The Times in 2018, producing and directing several episodes of the documentary series “The Weekly.” Her episode “The Myth of the Medallion,” which investigated the NYC taxi medallion bubble, was part of the project that won the 2020 Pulitzer Prize for Investigative Reporting. She has since produced and directed a number of documentaries for Netflix, Hulu, CNN, Vice and PBS, among other platforms.


Photo Credit: Alexis Johnson


Mac Schneider is based in Los Angeles and works across a range of reporter video formats, from visual explainers to news and enterprise.


Mac is an Emmy-nominated producer with more than a decade of experience developing and producing nonfiction projects, most recently as director of development at Concordia Studio. Prior to that, he was a senior producer at Vox, where he worked on both short- and longform projects, including “Explained” on Netflix and “Level Playing Field” on HBO, and as a member of Vox’s video team. He has reported on topics ranging from narcotrafficking at the U.S. border to soft power in sports to PFAS contamination to the opioid epidemic’s impact on American families.


Previously, Mac worked on documentary film projects for Netflix, VICE and HBO. He is a Seattle native and a graduate of Wesleyan University.


Edward Vega has covered culture in digital video for nearly a decade. After joining the Reporter Video team last year, where he collaborated with colleagues reviewing and reporting on topics ranging from film to music to lifestyle, he has transitioned to a new role as a cinematographer for the team. In this role, he’ll focus on maintaining the high caliber of cinematography for reporter videos while also driving innovation. Edward sits with Reporter Video and reports into Zach Caldwell, our manager of cinematography.


Before joining The Times, Edward was a senior video producer at Vox, where he produced explainer videos covering pop culture, science and cinema. His videos have amassed over 50 million collective views to date. Prior to Vox, Edward was a senior producer at Cheddar and Futurism, producing science and technology explainer videos and helping launch several narrative development projects.


Born and raised in Queens, Edward graduated from Queens College.


Welcome!


— Solana and Mona
